analysis: The only change in this PR is in a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ClusterInstalledSessionChecks/InstalledSessionCheck.swift. Head lines 984-986 extend the Gemma 4 adapter's expected rank environment in adaptersOnTheInstalledPath. The test now also expects a batch-lanes switch, DistributedInstalledPlan.batchLanesSwitch, set to String(DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes). That is a non-secret, fixed worker tuning value. The test's count and equality assertions at base lines 1002-1006 still bound the environment size, so the extra key is checked explicitly. The assertion at base lines 1029-1031 that adapter values cannot override the fixed ten environment values is unchanged; it requires the new key not to be among the reserved ones. I reviewed base units 4-6 and the single patch hunk. The test does not touch production code, so no trust boundary, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior changes. The cluster owner/worker path is outside the canonical threat model scope, and I saw nothing that touches TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or T-041. The production implementation of batchLanesSwitch and gemma4PipelineBatchLanes is not in the supplied evidence. Whether it keeps adapter environment keys from overriding fixed values, or from weakening the progress guard, is an unverified contract for any pass that sees the corresponding source change. This test change gives no evidence of a regression.
